title: Travessia or an international bank transfer?
label: Bank transfer
description: Compare getting paid through Travessia and by international bank transfer: costs, timing, rate and tax invoice, with a US$ 2,000 example.

short.title: Short answer
short.text: To receive US$ 2,000 from a client abroad, Travessia leaves R$ 10,834.60 in your account. A bank with a 4% spread and a US$ 45 fee leaves R$ 10,228.56. That is R$ 606.04 less per payment.
short.note: A bank can make more sense above US$ 50,000, where the spread is usually negotiated.

rows.label: Conversion cost
rows.them: 2% to 6% spread on the commercial rate

rows.label: Fee per payment
rows.them: US$ 15 to US$ 50, plus the intermediary bank fee

rows.label: When you convert
rows.us: Whenever you want, with the rate on screen
rows.them: On the day the exchange closes

rows.label: How your client pays
rows.us: Card or local transfer in their country

rows.label: Invoice and tax invoice
rows.us: English invoice and export nota fiscal in one flow

items.question: Do I need to close my bank account?
items.answer: No. Converted reais go to the account you already use, by Pix.

items.question: Does my client need to change anything?
items.answer: They pay through the Travessia invoice, by card or local transfer. No sign-up needed.

items.question: What about IOF?
items.answer: In most cases, payments for exported services have zero IOF. When there is IOF, it shows in the rate before you convert, in both cases.

breakdown.title: The numbers, step by step
breakdown.note: Spread and fees vary by bank and by client. Use the calculator to try your own numbers.
